newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Boots sees no OTC threat.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Boots sees no OTC threat.

text.p: British retail chemist Boots Co Plc said on Thursday it saw no threat to profits from a free-for-all in over-the-counter medicines if existing price regulation is scrapped.

Deputy chairman and chief executive Lord Blyth said in the past Boots The Chemist had always ended up taking market share and increasing cash margins whenever it has been subjected to price pressures.

He told Reuters in a telephone interview that if the existing price regulation was removed it would affect a relatively small percentage of over-the-counter medicines, which include headache pills, vitamins, and cold remedies.
"Less than five percent of Boots The Chemists' profits are represented by those products," Blyth said.
"As a threat to the profits of this business, frankly, despite all the furore on the subject, it is trivial."
Blyth said Boots had faced price cutting on sun creams, fragrances and condoms and had increased market share. "I can't think of any reason why it wouldn't be true of OTC medicines."

He said obviously the company was not complacent as OTC drugs were a key part of its business. But he said the lion's share was represented by Boots' own brand medicines and vitamins which were not covered by Resale Price Maintenance regulations.
Last month, Britain's competition watchdog the Office of Fair Trading said it would take legal action to remove fixed prices from over-the-counter medicines.
But a court decision on the issue is not expected before late 1997.
Blyth said the situation was still uncertain as the opposition Labour government has said it is not in favour of scrapping the price regulation.
"So you've got that additional complication that we could have a Labour government in power at the time," he said. A general election is due by May next year.

Boots said in a statement with its first half results it believed the price regulation should remain in force "because consumer interests are best served by retaining the service to local communities currently provided by pharmacists."
The company reported a 9.4 percent increase in pretax profits before exceptional items of 239.2 million stg.
Boots The Chemists made profits of 184.0 million stg, up from 164.3 million.
